seoTitle: How to Set Up Products & Prices in Stripe (2026)
metaDescription: Learn to create products in Stripe and add both one-time and recurring subscription prices, then connect them to checkout for your customers.
intro: Whether you're selling a single product or running a subscription business, Stripe's product and pricing setup is the foundation everything else builds on. This guide covers creating a new product, adding a one-time price, configuring a recurring subscription price, and understanding how those prices connect to customers and checkout.

steps.heading: Create a new product in Stripe
steps.body: Start by adding a product entry in your Stripe dashboard — this is the container that all your pricing options will attach to.

steps.heading: Add a one-time price type
steps.body: For simple, single-purchase items, configure a one-time price tied to the product you just created.

steps.heading: Set up recurring subscription pricing
steps.body: For memberships or SaaS-style billing, add a recurring price and choose the billing interval, such as monthly or annual.

steps.heading: Assign prices to customers and checkout
steps.body: Once your prices exist, connect them to your checkout flow or assign them directly to customers so billing actually happens.

faq.question: What's the difference between one-time and recurring prices in Stripe?
faq.answer: A one-time price charges a customer once, while a recurring price automatically bills them on a set interval, like monthly or yearly, until the subscription ends.

faq.question: Can one product have both a one-time and recurring price?
faq.answer: Yes, a single product in Stripe can have multiple price options attached, letting you offer both a one-time purchase and a subscription version.

faq.question: Do I need to write code to set up products and prices?
faq.answer: No, you can create products and prices directly from the Stripe dashboard without writing any code, then connect them to checkout.

faq.question: How do I bill customers on a monthly vs. annual cycle?
faq.answer: When creating a recurring price, you choose the billing interval, so you can set up separate monthly and annual price options for the same product.
